text: Thankfully, Singapore has not experienced such high-profile incidents relating to the breach of children’s digital privacy or adverse exposure to online harms.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: As avid users of technology, however, young people in Singapore are susceptible to such risks, even as we embrace the distinct benefits they can gain from the digital world.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Another key tranche to young people’s digital rights must, therefore, be ensuring access to digital literacy education to empower them with the skills to minimise digital risks and maximise gains.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: In this regard, Singapore has done well through efforts by the Ministry of Education (MOE), Ministry of Communications and Information, Infocomm Media Development Authority, National Library Board and the Media Literacy Council.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: I urge technology companies to do even more to support these public education efforts and consider the duty of care they owe to their young users.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Many have a digital footprint even before they have sprung from their mothers’ wombs, with their ultrasound images being shared on social media.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: That is but the beginning of their digital journey.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: In light of this prevailing reality, we must take concerted steps towards ensuring that children's digital rights are respected, supported and championed.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Indeed, given our extensive experience with digitalisation, Singapore can also be a key advocate of this movement on the world stage.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Such efforts will be in the best interests of the healthy and positive development of children in Singapore and beyond.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I stand in support of this Bill, which seeks to provide more extensive protection and better and fairer provisions for young persons up to the age of 18 in their best interests.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: There are cases where parents or guardians, in their fervour to bring out the best in their children, end up subjecting the child to emotional abuse or acts of degradation that erode the child’s feeling of self-worth, self-esteem or overall well-being.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Some parents see their scoldings and nagging or even acts of punishment as necessary acts of discipline for their children.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Where and how do we draw the line?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Do we intervene when a member of public complains?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Or do we wait until a significant adult in the child’s life, such as a school teacher or an adult relative, takes notice and informs the authorities?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Or do we need to wait until the child who is a victim of emotional or mental abuse speaks up or seeks help?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I seek clarification from the Ministry as to where and how do we draw the line with regard to a child or young person being in need of care or protection, as well as when do the authorities step in.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I am a parent, too, and I do understand the expectations some parents have on their children, in wanting them to realise their full potential and do well in school and later on in life.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: But we should not condone authoritarian or even authoritative parenting that revolves around scoldings or punishments or persistent nagging or acts of degradation, which are, essentially, abuse towards the child.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As a parent, love should always be the basis of our care and discipline towards our children.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We can certainly discipline our children and be firm with them in order to instil good values.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: But this should be done on the basis of love and care, and not on the basis of hate or wanting to inflict fear or pain.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Some children do suffer as a result of their parents' style of parenting.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: With these amendments, I hope more protection and the necessary care can be extended to the children or young persons who have otherwise been subjected to abuse or harm by those who should have been protecting them.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Within the last one year, I have had two families living within my constituency who came to seek help regarding their foster care arrangements.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: One of them, a couple with grandchildren, had been foster parents to a young girl since she was only a few weeks old.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The gentleman of this couple who are foster parents – let us call him Mr C – had alleged that the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) had acted in a biased and unfair manner towards him and his wife, and had, what he claimed, listened to and sided unfairly with the girl's biological father.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As a result, the girl was taken away from their foster care to be reunited with her biological father.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: He claimed that MSF had taken decisions on the matter "with no regard to the child's well-being".

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I had asked MSF to review the appeal made by Mr C to return the girl to his and his wife’s foster care.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: MSF had reviewed the case extensively and I learnt that it was Mr C's wife who had decided to discontinue care as a foster parent to the child in the first place.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Another couple, Mr S and his wife, have been foster parents with MSF for about nine years.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: They have cared for three children since then, with two of them still living in their care.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: A third child, the youngest of the three, was under their care for about six years, until he was removed from their care recently.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Mr S and his wife were distraught and claimed that MSF had taken the boy from their care with little notice and without considering their inputs and views on the matter.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: They also claimed that the boy did not want to return to his biological mother who had recently been released from prison.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Again, as expected, Mr S and his wife blamed MSF and claimed MSF had acted unfairly and did not consider the best interests of the child.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In both instances, I can fully understand the feelings of the foster parents.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: They had given their time, care and love towards the child they had fostered and cared for over several years.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And, inevitably, a strong emotional bond would have been formed between the foster parents and the child over those years.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: To let go of the child once their foster care is no longer needed is not an easy thing to do.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: At the same time, I must state my support for the work that MSF does.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As a Ministry, it has to look at each and every foster care case with objectivity and fairness, and in the best interest of the child in question.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: If possible, I would propose that the Minister include relevant professionals who would be able to provide significant inputs on the well-being of the child.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: These relevant professionals could be medical psychiatrists, clinical or child psychologists, school counsellors and educational professionals, among others.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I would also propose that this Committee consider for each foster case that is being contested or disputed, to interview the foster parents, the child or young person in question and biological parents to better understand their motivation for wanting a particular outcome pertaining to the foster case, even while they consider the report and recommendations made by MSF.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Eventually, these different inputs of important information can be put up as recommendations to the Court dealing with the particular foster case if need be.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Likewise, I would propose that where an order is made by a Youth Court, this Committee on Fostering is able to make recommendations to the Director-General of Social Welfare in deciding on any category 1, 2 or 3 matters relating to the child or young person, including the identification of a fit person to which the care of the child or young person is assigned.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Our foster parents also need the parental-related leave to care for their foster children.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: What forms of "mechanical restraints" are allowed to be used?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: To what extent are these mechanical restraints used?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And what if the mechanical restraints used inflict even more injury on the detainee than that it was first meant to prevent in the first place?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Hence, while I understand the need for restraints for violent or hostile behaviour, how does the Ministry decide, on a balance of probabilities and outcomes, when and what forms of mechanical restraints are to be used?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: At this juncture, Mr Deputy Speaker, please allow me to speak in Malay.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: (In Malay):   The challenges and issues faced by our community should not be taken lightly or are easily resolved.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Various factors can give rise to certain challenges or issues that affect a family, and its solutions can also include various factors and types of assistance.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: There is still room to further strengthen these solutions.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: M3 was established to specifically help families within our Malay/Muslim community and this also involves a collaboration with MSF.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This is a good initiative that has an encouraging and positive effect in strengthening our families, enhancing our skills and job opportunities, improving access to quality and affordable education, as well as rolling out initiatives that focus on our children’s well-being.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We must continue to support the Government’s objectives and initiatives like M3.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: (In English): Mr Deputy Speaker, the care of children and young persons who are removed from the care of their biological parents or from their foster parents, will always be a sensitive and emotive matter.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And where emotions run high, rationality and judgement may be clouded.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I do not envy the work of MSF in dealing with such sensitivities and I hope the amendments to CYPA will strengthen the provisions to be made, and for fairness and objectivity to prevail in ensuring the best interest of each child or young person in question.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Notwithstanding the clarifications I have sought earlier, I support this Bill.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is a step in the right direction.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I also applaud the extension of childcare leave to foster parents and urge parents to step forward to serve as foster parents.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: While our voluntary welfare organisations (VWOs) do their best in providing children who come through their doors with the best care possible, there is no substitute for a stable family environment.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Foster parents give children the stability, individual care and personal affection that they need, and I hope more people will step forward to become foster parents.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I will focus on our children's homes, which have been designated as a "place of safety" and our boys' home and girls' home.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Unfortunately, I have some residents who have been placed in a "place of safety", some of whom are only in primary schools.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My resident Allie, not her real name, has spent the last three years in a "place of safety".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have visited her there and I have to be honest that it was heartbreaking seeing her there.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: When I visited, a little boy was scaling the walls and the barbed wires trying to escape from the "place of safety".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The VWO was doing their absolute best in very difficult circumstances.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I used to take Allie out and she was a bubbly little girl, always running around and always with a big heart.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I used to take her out with my daughter, and I remember seeing her giving my daughter her black toy car.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They say those with the least give the most and this is so true.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Allie lived in a rental flat and did not have much, but she gave a lot, not just material gifts.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But she is someone who is so caring.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I remember my daughter coughing once and, almost instinctively, Allie would pat my daughter's back to make her feel better.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: A few months after Allie was sent to a "place of safety", the Allie I knew vanished and was replaced by a quiet reserved girl who barely spoke a word.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This was despite all the hard work the social workers and case manager had put in to help her.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She changed completely and I could see why.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She was taken away from her house, her siblings, her family and even her school.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Everything she knew of and was used to, was removed from her.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I know we do this to protect her, to help her.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But we need to start questioning whether this works.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Again, let me put on record that I commend the VWOs for doing a very admirable job of caring for the children with limited resources.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: At the same time, I believe we can and we have to do more for children like Allie and her siblings who just need a nurturing environment to grow and blossom.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In the spirit of protecting and rehabilitating our vulnerable children, I have the following questions and recommendations on helping VWOs which run "places of safety".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We place all the children together, all of whom are angry, sad, lost, frustrated, disappointed and I do not think it helps when they are placed together with insufficient support.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand that staff and resource constraints are a perpetual problem that VWOs have to grapple with.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I had the same problem, too, when running my VWO.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But in the best interest of our children, we should ensure that our VWOs are adequately staffed and have the resources they need to do their work.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Are there plans to further reduce the current ratio to ensure that each child has sufficient individualised care and attention?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Does MSF have plans to provide more funding to VWOs running a "place of safety"?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Next, Allie and her two siblings were housed in "places of safety".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They were sent there on the same day but were separated as the "place of safety" Allie was sent to did not have a place for her two brothers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: While I understand the logistical constraints, it brings about acute stress for a child to be separated from siblings, especially when they have already lost their parents.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Children in crisis are at their most vulnerable.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They feel fear, confusion, abandonment, worry and sadness.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is essential that they receive quick support and care, in stable conditions they can feel comfortable in.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Keeping Allie and her siblings together is the least we could do to create stability under such turbulent circumstances.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This will help the VWOs running our "places of safety" as well.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In determining custody, care and control of the children in divorce cases, the Court has stated that siblings should not be separated as far as possible.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Court considers this to be a factor in considering the welfare of the children.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Next, Allie was also removed from her school as they wanted to send her to a school nearer to the "place of safety".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But I hope that we can allow a child to remain in his or her school after they have been sent to a "place of safety".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I cannot imagine how difficult it must have been for Allie to go to a new primary school, try to make new friends, maybe even answer questions by her classmates on why she is there and, I hope not, but maybe even be laughed at.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I hope that MSF will consider this recommendation positively.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Next, inter-generational patterns of incarceration is a recognised phenomenon.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Breaking this vicious cycle has been included as a goal in many efforts to support inmates and ex-offenders in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For example, addressing the inter-generational offending cycle is a key objective of Family Resource Centres, which support inmates' families.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This pattern of incarceration can start at an early age.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Whilst children's homes are intended to be safe places for the protection of vulnerable children, the roots of inter-generational incarceration may also begin here.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We will not know until we have studied this problem.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In putting Allie in a "place of safety", we took her away from her home, her siblings and everything that she was used to.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We put her in a dormitory and expect her to be rehabilitated and helped in the process.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Do we know whether doing this will lead to better outcomes for the children?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have seen how Allie has changed from her time at the "place of safety" and it breaks my heart.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And I know this has not worked for her brother.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We need data to measure the effectiveness of our programmes and ensure that our policies work and work well.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We need to provide more help to the VWOs which run our "places of safety".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand this is intended to prevent children in the homes from escaping custody or inflicting bodily injury on themselves.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This seems incompatible with our shift to a more rehabilitative approach.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand that there might be circumstances where there is a genuine need to physically restrain the children.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Our children's homes are already staffed by Auxiliary Officers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They are in a better position to step in, if necessary.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: There should be a clear distinction between the roles of the staff and Auxiliary Officers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Staff of the children's homes should be nurturing figures who are there to protect, not restrain the children.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Imagine the psychological effect on children to see the staff using handcuffs on them and their friends.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Children who are put in "places of safety" because of circumstances beyond their control have the same potential as any other child, and are no less deserving of care and attention.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Let us make sure that we can give them the safe environment to break free of their unfortunate circumstances and to grow into their full potential.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Let us make sure we help the children and also improve support and resources provided to the VWOs running our "places of safety".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Notwithstanding the above queries and recommendations, I stand in support of this Bill.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: First off, on behalf of foster parents, I would like to thank MSF for allowing foster parents to benefit from childcare leave.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: This is something that many in the VWO space, including myself, have asked for.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Second, over the years, we are aware of good progress that MSF and our VWOs have made to resource our homes that serve our vulnerable children and youths.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: As such, I would like MSF to comment on the current state of affairs.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Have we seen a decrease over the years?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Most of us will agree that family-based care is a better model compared to home-based care for children and youths, as long as the foster or adopted parents have the means and the care and concern for them.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Therefore, can MSF share whether we have been able to put more of these children and youths into family-based care situations, such as through adopted and foster parents?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Thirdly, can MSF share on how more we can encourage more people to move forward as foster parents?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: I understand that there is a certain number of Singaporeans who would like to adopt children.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Is there room for us to encourage them to consider fostering instead?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Next, is there a way for us to streamline the adoption process so as to reduce the cost of adoption?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: On the ground, I see some cases of grandparents from the sandwich class who want to adopt their grandchildren because the parents are not able or available to provide care.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: And the legal cost takes precious resources away from the grandparents.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Lastly, under CYPA, we have expanded on the definition of "emotional harm" to include "danger to oneself or to other persons", and "severely withdrawn, anxious or depressed".

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: In this context, there is one particular group of children and youths I would like to talk about, that is, those with extreme online addiction that has handicapped their ability to cope with life.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: On the ground, I have seen a few of these cases who suffered such situations.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Recently, I had a distressed parent coming in regarding this person's son who has suffered severe online addiction issues.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: The secondary school youth has stopped going to school, has gone beyond parental control and has started exhibiting violent behaviour.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: The youth's school and parents were not able to persuade this youth to go back to school.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Yet, because this youth has not committed a crime, has not yet done something that is deemed as traditionally high risk, the mandatory intervention mechanism could not kick in.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: In this case, for this resident, what I did was we brought in a volunteer who was a game developer and we tried to go in and persuade this person that if he likes to game, maybe he can be a game developer one day and, from then on, we try to encourage him to go back to school.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: In all likelihood, the online addiction may be rooted or compounded by other behaviours, emotional or even mental issues.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: But a mandatory therapy will give us a chance to diagnose the situation and do the necessary course correction.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I draw my suggestions from my co-labourers and volunteers, and my experience serving the CYPs in my constituency, district and in the special needs sector I have three areas for the Ministry to consider further strengthening in order to reap better outcomes.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: First, to strengthen the coordination and integration of care for these children; second, to strengthen the voice of the children and young persons; and third, to strengthen the foster parents' scheme.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: First, strengthening the coordination and integration of care.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Despite the immense many efforts by volunteers and agency staff, I found the outcomes for these children at risk and young persons at risk are often still less than ideal.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: It is definitely not for lack of heart and hands because I know how much each volunteer and staff care and put in.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: These partners on the ground have told me the following needs that, if better addressed, would surely improve the life outcomes for the young people they care for.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: These needs are: one, the need for a safe environment where children feel secure; where they can learn and even rest without a constant heightened feeling of fear, anxiety and disruption.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Such an environment can be found in both mainstream and special schools; but much depends on the kindness of the adults in charge.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: In the mainstream First Toa Payoh Primary School, there is a programme called Home @ School to provide such a safe environment for after-school.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: In the special school Pathlight where I volunteer, the OHANA after-school programme offers such a safe setting.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The second need is the need for a constant and familiar adult supervision which can come in the form of teachers, youth workers, social workers or foster parents.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: One of the key challenges to track and address, for instance, is the turnover of such adult supervisors in the lives of these children and young persons causing further disruptions in their lives.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The third is the need for better and constant access to needed community and healthcare, including mental healthcare, services.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: In many instances, the different help agencies and staff hardly have time to meet physically nor update regularly and communicate with one another until something happens in the life of these young persons.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Each of them working within their own scope of duty and doing their very best – the youth worker taking care of the youth services for the young; the drug counsellor taking care of a parent; the social service officers delivering financial assistance.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Without an appointed solution integrator to deliver more effective case management, I fear that the lives of the children and young persons will experience a spiral downwards.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: One young boy I know has already turned to smoking and dating at Primary 6 after losing both parents.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Another young girl I know whose mother is in remand for drug offences became worse off when there was no effective handshake between her counsellors as she transited from primary to secondary school.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: One student with special needs I know very well is facing transition challenges and he is preparing to leave school after special school.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The second need is this: to strengthen the voice of the CYPs.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Deputy Speaker, Sir, I have mixed feelings as I go through the Bill.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: On one hand, it is a comprehensive one covering many needed gaps.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: On the other hand, I cannot help but feel that in our efforts to protect the child, we are seeing things a lot through the lenses of the adult and not enough through the eyes of the CYPs we are trying to help.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: How do we incorporate the voice of these young people whose lives we attempt to shape for the better?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: In matters that impact them, such as the change of school; admission into children’s homes or foster homes; in identifying their adult supervisors, are there measures installed to take into account the feelings and preferences of these young persons?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: How can the long and onerous process of gathering evidence, determination and implementation of Court orders for children caught in parental disputes, the process be improved so that their feelings are considered?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: In the new section 68(A), for instance, that authorises the use of "mechanical restraint", such as handcuffs or leg braces on a child or young person, how do we ensure that the least damage is done on them?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Are affected children and young persons involved in the numerous decisions made for them incorporated in this Bill?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I have a few suggestions for the Ministry to consider to strengthen this important scheme.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This is especially with regard to raising the age limit for protection from abuse or neglect from the age of below 16 to below 18.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Those who are within this age group can be very impressionistic and be quite easily swayed by adults.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Sometimes, they are unable to comprehend the wider implications of their decisions which may result in their underestimating the risks of their actions or behaviours.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: And this group of our young can be exploited by criminals and we have also seen how girls and boys alike have fallen victim to sexual predators.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: What is the current ratio of officers to youths at risk?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Is there an ideal ratio from the professional standpoint?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Also, under the Enhanced Care and Protection Order (ECPO), a Court order may authorise a person other than the child's natural parents or guardians to care and make decisions for the child.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: As the Order will provide the caregivers with powers to make decisions for the child which would otherwise require parental consent, who are the caregivers that the Ministry has on its list, and would this be expanded further?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Would the passage of this Bill require a new team to be set up within the Ministry to handle such cases?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: (In Malay):   Another point that I wish to raise is whether the Ministry would ensure that the person under the caregiver would not be coerced, for instance, to convert to a particular religion.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This is important, especially in multiracial Singapore, because there may be caregivers who are over-enthusiastic in trying to promote their own religion, and perhaps this is done with good intentions, but they should respect the fact that the child should be allowed to make his/her own decision after reaching 18 years of age.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Having spoken to people in the relevant field of work like welfare, I also note that differing values and certain biases are among some factors that could lead to unfair implementation of ECPO or the possibility that it will not be used.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: My other concern is that we could compromise the structure and integrity of families by being overzealous in interfering with the discipline and care of children.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: What does taking an 18-year-old away from his/her parents say about or have a negative impact on their worth as parents?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: What does it tell the youth about his relationship with his parents?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Can he still respect his parents after that?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Are we sowing the seeds of rebellion against his parents in the future?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Or is there something about the parent-child relationship that should be protected, regardless of how bad the parents are at parenting?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: At the very least, we should have some mechanism or provision to show that we value the rights of the parents.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We do not want to cultivate a parenting culture that is afraid to discipline their children when the need arises.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I hope that we can focus more on counselling both children and parents, and that taking away parents’ rights should only be the last resort, or if their actions endanger the child's life or have lasting severe impact on the child.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I would believe that, in such cases, the parent would be facing criminal charges.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Are they aware that their rights as a parent are being taken away in their case?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: How might they mount a defence against the implied charge that they are incompetent and incapable parents?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Areas of interest would include household income, family structure, primary caregiver, ethnicity and so on, so that we have greater insights on possible factors that cause the issues between parent and child, and we can then tackle the issues more appropriately.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Can the Minister share what is in place in the system to ensure that there is no clash of cultural values?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: While thus far we are addressing the issue of protection, I hope attention would also be given to counselling these young persons to help them cope emotionally with their circumstances when the Ministry intervenes.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Often, the circumstances under which the young are facing, especially in the case of parents who are estranged and divorced, can be a trauma.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Next, I would like to touch on the caregivers for the young, especially when they are under the charge of grandparents who may not only be aged but may not have a good grasp of the English language to be able to give appropriate guidance to those under their charge.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, when it comes to making decisions, especially on educational matters, the aged grandparents may not be able to make that value-added decision.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Additionally, the grandparents may also not have the financial resources to support the young to pay for the courses that they think best suit the child.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Although 17- or 18-year-olds are likely to possess the intellectual capabilities of making informed decisions, this does not mean that they possess the same level of emotional and psychological maturity as an adult to make those decisions.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And I am sure that there are many parents of such young people who would agree with me.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As such, the question is whether or not 17- and 18-year-olds should be treated as an adult when decisions need to be made regarding their safety and welfare are highly pertinent ones.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Indeed, research has shown that while youths and adults may possess almost the same level of intellectual capabilities, youths are, however, less able than adults to make mature decisions that may have important outcomes in their lives.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: One aspect of increasing the age of protection would be the need to extend a duty of care to a greater number of older youths who are sent to Government homes for various reasons.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Physically, these older youths may be of the same physical build of adults, but they will likely lack the emotional and mental maturity of adults.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I would thus like to ask what are some of the measures that the Government could put in place to ensure that the mental and emotional well-being of these older youths are taken care of.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Also, would Government-run homes have the necessary incident management standard operating procedures to manage older youths, as they would likely require a different set of management procedures when they get into incidents compared to younger children who might get into similar incidents during their stay at the homes?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Emotional and psychological abuse have long-term impact on individuals and the extent of the harm caused by psychological and emotional trauma is arguably more significant and last longer than physical abuse.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As compared to an "injury" which requires perhaps professional assessments and objective evidence to substantiate that victims have suffered from hurt or trauma, "harm" seems to suggest a lower establishment threshold before interventions can be implemented.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This begets the question of who will determine whether or not children are at risk of harm and to what extent "harm" must be proven before interventions can be implemented.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: With the potential expansion in the level of intervention that needs to be implemented, does the Government possess sufficient resources to ensure that all victims of emotional and psychological harm are thus provided with a sufficient level of support to avert the long-term impact of such harm?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: With the increased need to provide step-up care to a larger number of children and youths, and the demand for greater resources to support more victims of abuse and harm, it seems likely that the Government will need to increase staff resources to ensure that there is a sufficient number of professionals who can provide interventions to children.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I would thus like to urge the Government to concurrently enhance the capabilities of staff who are already working in Government-run homes for children and strengthen the capabilities of those homes to provide holistic care.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As such, could the Government consider reviewing the knowledge, skills, abilities and other competencies of professionals who are working with children, enhance the career prospects of the profession and perhaps even reconsider the remuneration and benefits of these professionals to attract a larger number, especially potential mid-career switchers, to enter this field?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We need to ensure that we are able to entice and retain more people with the right passion to enter this field.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The Government could also perhaps consider tapping on those looking for re-employment, perhaps full-time parents or even grandparents who are looking to return to the workforce.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: If these happen to be parents or grandparents of children and youths of a similar age, they could likely have the aptitude and skillsets to successfully work with these children and at-risk youths.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This gesture is a significant one, and I am sure that it will be well-received as the childcare leave will accord them greater flexibility at work for them to provide the necessary care for the children they are fostering.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Emotional bonds between foster parents and the fostered child will inevitably grow over time.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I would imagine that it would be emotionally painful for a set of foster parents to be separated from their foster child once the child reaches a certain age or when the foster child leaves their foster parents to go back to his or her biological homes.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I thus end my speech in firm support of this Bill.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: It should be an inalienable right of every Singaporean baby.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Yet, for some children, they are not exactly equals because of family circumstances.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: For example, children under the care of foster parents or unwed mothers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Singapore needs to keep reviewing its policies to support people and families in different circumstances.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Over the years, we have made headway in supporting them.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Now, all mothers are given the 16-week maternity leave, as well as a Child Development Account.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: These enhancements show that the Government is prepared to make changes to support our young families, regardless of the constitution of their families.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The move to support foster parents is another positive evolution.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Foster parents are important in the network of support for vulnerable children.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: They are no different from the children's natural parents in having to balance their careers and families.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: It is not uncommon for the next of kin to take care of children neglected or abandoned by parents, or if there is a sudden bereavement.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Will these kin-carers also be covered in the Bill?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The Labour Movement has been a strong advocate to improve support given to families.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: We are happy that the Government has responded to the call over the years and have now progressed to the foster parents.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: As we note this important progression in this Bill, let us also not forget to continue to work towards helping our unwed mothers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: In 2013, the Labour Movement advocated for the Government to accord the same level of benefits that married mothers get to unwed mothers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: First, we should revisit allowing unwed mothers to purchase Housing and Development Board (HDB) flats before 35 years old.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Housing is a practical issue that families must deal with.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: This means that unwed mothers will have to rent a place if they are not living with their family or relatives, increasing the cost burden on such families, on top of the cost of raising children.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Can we reconsider this fundamental need for lodging as they are often younger, and allow concession in consideration of their plight and circumstances, to purchase a flat even before the mother turns 35?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Today, unwed mothers are not eligible for such relief.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Since they also work productively, providing to society, there seem to be reasons for them to be included for such reliefs as well.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: They need to be given opportunities to learn to express themselves, to make responsible decisions, and to participate in processes that affect their well-being and their future, according to their age and maturity.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The extension of the protection from 16 to 18 years old and greater support to caregivers are positive steps to creating a kinder and more supportive environment.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: First, I note that several Members of Parliament were concerned that the power to protect abused or neglected children could overly interfere with how parents legitimately discipline and raise their children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Christopher de Souza touched on the definition of "emotional harm".

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For example, Mr Christopher de Souza asked what infantilisation is, in one of the examples.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This occurs when a parent or guardian deliberately treats a child as being much younger than a child's actual age and, in a way, that is not developmentally appropriate for the child.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For example, say, a child in upper primary school being made to wear diapers every day.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Member also asked about the example of being confined in a small space.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: By that, we refer to a space that is not conducive for the child's development and is beyond socially-accepted boundaries for punishment, for example, locking a child in a cage, the toilet, the storeroom as a form of punishment.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I wish to assure Members that we do not intend to diminish parental authority.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We do not intend to unduly intervene with parents' rights to discipline their children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And we do not intend to overly intrude into the private lives of families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The vast majority of parents are responsible and do their best to care for and raise their children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Within the private lives of families, within the bounds of parental authority, there is a wide berth or space for parents to nurture, raise and discipline their children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The common adage goes: "Spare the rod, spoil the child." But unfortunately, a small number struggle to parent responsibly, for whatever reason.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And when parenting or so-called discipline crosses the line and becomes excessively harsh or abusive, whether physically or emotionally, we may have to intervene to protect the children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Louis Ng, Er Dr Lee Bee Wah, Ms Anthea Ong and Mr Christopher de Souza spoke about the impact of removing children from families and asked whether MSF could provide a sense of continuity and familiarity to children who have been placed in out-of-home care.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: When we receive reports that raise concerns about the safety of children, we first undertake a comprehensive social investigation.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Often, our social services move in, rather immediately, the Child Protective Service.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We look at factors, such as the context, intentions, severity, persistence of the abuse or neglect, likelihood of future harm to the child and the strengths and as well as the needs of the families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In doing so, we are aided by evidence-based assessment tools.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Our Child Protection Officers are sensitive to the emotions that may overwhelm the child and are trained to apply trauma-informed practices when interviewing children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We also consult professionals, such as psychologists and psychiatrists, when needed.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Police may concurrently investigate if a criminal offence is reported or suspected to have taken place.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Our efforts focus on keeping the family intact with safety plans in place.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But when the home environment is unsafe for the child, MSF may have to remove the child from his parents as a last resort.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We then work quickly to ensure that the child can be placed in a safe place, whether under the care of his grandparents or other relatives, such as aunts and uncles, foster parents or a children's home.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: When the child is in out-of-home care, these caregivers who may be extended family members will be able to make decisions for the child in a timely manner.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: MSF will also work closely with professionals in the child's network of support, such as school counsellors and teachers, to review the child's progress from time to time.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: When needed, we may consult independent panels, such as the Committee on Fostering, which comprises a range of professionals from the relevant fields, such as education, child psychology and psychiatry.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will facilitate constant contact between the child and family members where possible to maintain that important relationship.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Family reunification, after all, remains the long-term goal for many children in state care.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Court may also order the parents to attend counselling or other programmes to ensure the well-being and safety of the child and also make orders to assist the child in recovery.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For example, MSF does not charge for the services we provide to the families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Our appointed social service agencies also have arrangements to keep their services well accessible to families, regardless of their socio-economic status.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Now, I will share the policy considerations behind how we place children in out-of-home care.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Henry Kwek and Ms Denise Phua, for example, spoke about fostering.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The reality is that we do not have enough foster parents for every child in need of protection.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As a foster parent, you have to open not only your hearts but also open your homes.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This challenge is especially so for older children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: There are also children with more complex needs whose interests are better served in a residential care setting.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Louis Ng and Ms Anthea Ong spoke about sibling groups in out-of-home care – sometimes, a pair; sometimes, many more.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: MSF strives to place siblings together as far as possible.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Doing so preserves their relationships and allows them to support each other through difficult times.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And yet, sometimes, we have to split them up.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have to consider the circumstances of each case, manage within the realities of our out-of-home care landscape.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Even though siblings may not stay together in some instances, MSF and our partners will facilitate contact between the siblings as well as with their natural parents.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Louis Ng also spoke about school arrangements.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: MSF is guided by what is in the child's best interest.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Where the expected duration of the out-of-home care placement is short or the child will soon be taking a national exam, or the current school provides good support for his needs, we prefer to let the child continue in his current school.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: If a change of school is in the interest of the child, MSF will work with the schools, the foster families or children's homes to help with the transitions.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In the case of Allie referred to in Mr Louis Ng's speech, the change of school was done for her benefit.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The distance between the home and the original school meant very long and tiring daily commutes for her, and that showed when she returned to the home.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: My colleagues have recently checked on Allie and I am told that she is progressing well in her placement, despite initial adjustment difficulties.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And we understand that she was caught between a rock and a hard place.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Her family situation was none the better and that is why she had to be removed in the very first place.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will monitor the girl's situation and work towards reunifying her with her family.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat was concerned that it may undermine the rights of parents, quite similar to the first set of questions that I addressed.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: When a child has been placed in out-of-home care, we seek to return the child back to his family as soon as possible.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Caveat: if it is safe to do so.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Hence, before applying for an ECPO, MSF and our community partners would already have sought to reunify the family.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This includes providing counselling and psychotherapy, identifying responsible adults in the family to anchor possible safety plans and preparing the relevant touchpoints in the community, such as schools and preschools, to play a part in those plans.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Our practice is to try to place children with foster families of the same race and religion as far as possible or, if that is not possible due to fostering constraints, we will consult and seek parental consent.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Our children’s homes operate on a secular basis, while providing for the religious needs of the child, including other requirements, such as dietary needs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Darryl David and Mr Henry Kwek asked about fostering and adoption.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: While this Bill, in itself, does not touch on adoption, foster parents may apply to adopt the children under the Adoption of Children Act.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Adoption of a foster child may be considered if it is in the welfare of the child.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This is if the natural parents are unable or unwilling to care for the child or will significantly compromise the safety and well-being of the child.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will take the Members' feedback on facilitating the adoption of children in state care into consideration when we review our laws and processes on that Act.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Ms Anthea Ong asked whether income tax benefits can be given to foster families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Foster parents face caregiving challenges, similar to natural parents.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Financially, foster parents receive fostering allowances to defray expenses for the children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The quantum is higher if the children have special needs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: They also get childcare and medical subsidies to assist them.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Ms Anthea Ong and Mr Desmond Choo also spoke about supporting other caregivers in caring for abused or neglected children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Some Members spoke about amendments relating to the rehabilitation of youth offenders.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Youth justice in Singapore is premised on gradated intervention.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Our approach is to try to divert youth offenders, including those between the ages of 16 and 18, away from the Court wherever possible.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Youth offenders who are not diverted are assessed whether they are suitable for probation.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Probation focuses on community-based rehabilitation and the Court may order accompanying conditions depending on the needs of the youths.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This means that youths who are required to reside in places of detention and juvenile rehabilitation centres (JRCs) generally have higher risk behaviours, more complex needs or a weak family environment that does not support rehabilitation.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And that tends to manifest in their behaviour and in their interactions with other people.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Earlier, I had explained that we need to strike a good balance between helping youth offenders rehabilitate and reintegrate into society on the one hand and ensuring the safety of residents and staff in places of detention and juvenile rehabilitation centres, and of the public in general.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, this brings me to my next point, on how we seek to achieve such a balance.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Ms Sylvia Lim asked about the treatment of youth suspects and youth offenders, by law enforcement officers, MSF and the Courts.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Ms Sylvia Lim correctly pointed out that there are existing laws and protocols that law enforcement officers must adhere to when handling youth suspects, such as not detaining arrested persons for more than 48 hours.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The law enforcement officers, such as the Police, are trained to handle youth suspects.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Where feasible, the Police try to expedite the investigation of cases involving youth suspects.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Police protocols also involve the activation of Appropriate Adults to support the emotional needs of young suspects and to ensure close coordination between law enforcement and other agencies, such as schools and MSF, for appropriate follow-up.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Appropriate Adults and the Police are trained to look out for signs of distress by youths during the interview and can assess if the youth is in a suitable condition or state to be interviewed or not.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Police Officer can also decide to discontinue the interview and reschedule the interview when the young suspect is in a more stable emotional state.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: After investigations, a decision on whether to release and divert the youth, or proceed with a charge, is made.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We also recognise that some youths, especially older youths, may commit serious offences and can be repeat offenders.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This is where the Public Prosecutor as well as the Youth Court have the discretion to charge the offender in either the Youth Court or a Court of appropriate jurisdiction, such as the State Courts.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Youth Court, in making any order, must consider the needs of each youth and their risks of reoffending in future.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Youth Court typically calls for a pre-sentencing report to determine if the youth is suitable for probation or otherwise and weighs several factors, such as whether the youth has prior offences, the youth's behaviour in school, his relationship with peers, family circumstances, the availability and strength of familial and community support, are also important.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Where there is adequate supervision, appropriate discipline and consistent parenting are also considered.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: After taking into consideration the risks and the needs of the youth, the Court can order a youth offender to undergo rehabilitation under a probation order or in a JRC.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In considering whether a youth requires reformative training, the Court would call for a suitability report to determine whether the youth's physical and mental condition are suitable for a Reformative Training Centre.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Youth Court would also consider whether the youth has demonstrated aggressive or violent behaviour, such as when the youth was remanded at the MSF Youth Homes.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The youth may be assessed to have such a high risk of aggressive behaviour that it may not be safe for the youth to be detained in the JRC, especially if it may affect the safety or disrupt the rehabilitation of other youths in the JRC.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The assessment of individual risk levels and the needs of the youth determines the regime and environment that best support his rehabilitation.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Hence, in incidents involving more than one youth, it may be possible that the Youth Court may grant different orders as is needed for their rehabilitation.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: At the same time, parity in sentencing is vital to preserve and protect public confidence in the way justice is administered.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: While he was at the Singapore Boys’ Home, he repeatedly threatened youth guidance officers and intimidated other residents.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: He is burly, well-built at about 1.83 metres tall, a head taller than I am, and, in one instance, he held his dormitory mate by the neck and lifted him off the ground, choking him.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Fortunately, the staff witnessed it and intervened immediately.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And this is one out of many scenarios where our officers find it essential to be able to deploy the use of restraints and other measures quickly to safeguard other residents.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Members may be aware that a serious incident took place at the Singapore Boys' Home last year.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Though all three officers are back at their workplace, we must reduce the risks of such incidents repeating.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I have described the complexity and the behaviours of the youths who are residing in the JRC.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Because it is a rehabilitative environment, we have many youth guidance officers, psychologists, counsellors and therapists who need a safe environment to provide that rehabilitative support.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Other youths there also need to be assured of their safety.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Darryl David asked, therefore, whether we have the capability to handle older and bigger-built youths and much taller youths in MSF's Youth Homes.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Ms Rahayu Mahzam and Ms Anthea Ong asked about the necessity of mechanical restraints.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I think almost all Members raised this issue and I can understand your concern.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Like I mentioned yesterday, they will not be used as a punitive measure.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But Members will appreciate that there are, indeed, real-life situations where the use of such restraints is necessary to prevent escalation, escape or harm.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Youth home staff will attempt to verbally de-escalate tensions, calm down any aggressive residents and persuade them to cease aggressive behaviours.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: When suitable, the Youth Homes also use therapy or padded rooms to help calm agitated residents down.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: If a youth remains aggressive or the situation escalates despite our efforts to calm him down, MSF Youth Home staff will first verbally issue a warning.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And if the youth persists, MSF staff will apply de-escalation techniques based on their training on management of actual or potential aggression (MAPA), as mentioned by Ms Anthea Ong yesterday.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Only when absolutely necessary will our officers use restraints to manage the resident so as to minimise risks of injury to other residents or staff.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As far as possible, it would be the Auxiliary Police Officers who will do so.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But Mr Louis Ng will understand that, in some instances, given the situation, our officers may also have to respond to take appropriate action for the safety of residents and staff.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: MSF will put in place stringent procedures and processes in the use of restraints.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This includes recording each use of the restraint and removing the restraint once the need has passed.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, after the restraints are removed, an MSF officer will help the resident to process his feelings and, where necessary, a multidisciplinary team comprising the case worker, psychologist and psychiatrist will also support the youth through this process.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Our aim is to provide a safe and secure environment for all residents and staff in MSF Youth Homes to facilitate rehabilitation.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Some Members asked about the management of youths of different ages.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: When we raised the age limit to below 18 at point of admission, some youths may remain in our care or custody till they are about 21 years old.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: There are various considerations in how we group the residents in the MSF Youth Homes.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Given the differing levels of maturity, the young ones are generally housed separately from the older youths at the MSF Youth Homes.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As the older youths are at a different stage of development from the existing younger youths, our officers need to have adequate training and experience to address the different risks and needs of older youths.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This includes being able to supervise and guide the youths in day-to-day activities, such as attending educational classes or playing sports in a group setting.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This helps the youths to gain soft skills, which are important in interacting with youths of different ages.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Ultimately, our intent is to facilitate their rehabilitation and reintegration with family and society at large.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Many Members like Mr Desmond Choo spoke about providing support for families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In particular, Er Dr Lee Bee Wah, Ms Anthea Ong and Ms Denise Phua spoke about providing early support for at-risk families, before their situations worsen.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Vulnerable individuals and families sometimes face complex challenges and require the support of multiple agencies and community organisations to help them regain stability.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: MSF has been working with our partners to transform our social services, integrate service delivery and strengthen last-mile support.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The objective is to provide more comprehensive, convenient and coordinated support for these families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have also made significant investment in the early childhood sector to give every child a good start in life and to support families with young children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The KidSTART programme provides support for child development, coordinates and strengthens services for families where needed and monitors the developmental progress of children from birth.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These will support parents to become more confident in their parenting, reduce parental stress and better manage negative behaviour in their children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Henry Kwek and Prof Lim Sun Sun spoke about digital wellness and online addiction.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
