text: There are programmes in the community for families facing such challenges, such as the National Addictions Management Service (NAMS) which provides treatment for persons with gaming or Internet addictions.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Community agencies, such as Fei Yue Community Service and TOUCH Community Services, conduct programmes to support children, including teaching them coping strategies to manage their gaming activity.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Statutory intervention and legal enforcement should not be the only or "go to" approach.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As far as possible, our families should be supported by the community.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Ms Sylvia Lim asked whether families and children have the right to be heard before the Youth Court.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: She also wanted to know what options are available for children and families who are unable to engage lawyers.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This is why we have programmes that divert youth offenders away from the Court system and why we are requiring families to attend the mandatory family programme before applying for an FGO.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But for cases that are before the Court, it is important to keep the law accessible and easy to understand.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: There are provisions in the Act and in the Bill to ensure that the child's or his parents' voices are heard during proceedings.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Section 42 of CYPA also provides that where a child is brought before the Youth Court, it is the Court’s duty to explain the substance of the offence to the child in a language suitable for his age and understanding.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Moreover, for child protection cases, MSF case workers are guided by the best interests of the child.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Similarly, for FGO cases, a counsellor will work with the family through their difficulties.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These professionals help to safeguard the interests of the child and the family.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Exceptionally, if the presence of lawyers is necessary, there are avenues of assistance available for those who are not able to afford lawyers.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: They may seek assistance from the Law Society's Pro Bono Services or legal clinics run by various community, religious and social service agencies.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Criminal legal aid is also available through the Criminal Legal Aid Scheme (CLAS) for children and young persons who are accused of a crime or an offence.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Community Justice Centre (CJC) also assists litigants in person.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For example, CJC runs a scheme when an assigned Court Friend provides practical and emotional support and the Court Friend may provide information on Court procedures and explain the Judge's instructions to the child or parent.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We consulted many stakeholders, including our social service agencies, members of the Youth Advisory Group and so on.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: They have told us that they need to build capacity and capabilities to manage both a higher number of children, as well as older youths with differing needs and risks.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: MSF will ensure that all our community partners and agencies are given sufficient time to work through their plans and processes, so that we are collectively ready to implement these changes.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Members, such as Ms Rahayu Mahzam, Mr Louis Ng, Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Mr Darryl David, also spoke about our ability to manage the larger number of children who will be covered under the Act.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I assure Members that we have been planning and working on building capacity and capability to enable us to be ready to implement these changes.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The preparations are ongoing, but will take time and additional resources.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Our community partners have emphasised the need to prepare and to be ready.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I have explained that it takes time to strengthen the safety and security within MSF's Youth Homes.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We need to make changes to infrastructure to enable age-appropriate rehabilitation and expand the existing academic and vocational curriculum that is provided.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We also need to strike the right balance, to provide an environment that is safe for residents and staff and conducive for rehabilitation in the Youth Homes.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Ms Rahayu Mahzam and Mr Louis Ng spoke about the data and research that inform us about our programmes and our policies.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This is, in part, because of our efforts to increase greater awareness, such as the Break the Silence campaign, and people have been able to identify cases more easily, to speak out against violence; and better detection of child abuse cases using screening tools and processes.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For example, we developed the Child Abuse Reporting Guide (CARG) that is used by our partners, such as childcare centres, schools and medical professionals, to guide them on what to look out for in detecting child abuse.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The findings inform the work that we do, for example, through the National Committee on Prevention, Rehabilitation and Recidivism (NCPR), that I co-chair with Minister Josephine Teo from the Ministry of Home Affairs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will continue to track data and outcomes in relation to abuse, neglect and offending.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Third, for families that require guidance in parenting, the Bill would help strengthen family relationships and better guide parenting of children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: At the same time, our work with vulnerable children cannot be accomplished by legislation alone.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Only when we work collectively as a community can we help our vulnerable children overcome their difficult circumstances to have the best shot in life.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I also appreciate the policy officers and the legal officers for working hard on this Bill.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This Bill, if Parliament supports, is a result of their hard work and their recommendations borne out of many years of experience.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I wonder if he could comment on whether the Ministry observes that cases where the authorities have had to intervene with alternative care arrangements, is this a phenomenon that is predominantly found in those with lower income?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: And related to that, is there any indication that it is actually a resource issue that has led to these problems and, in that sense, support of the family may have to be on a wider basis and perhaps even earlier before these problems arise?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This includes well-to-do families who may have issues that prevent them from ensuring the safety of their children.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These could include mental health issues, spousal conflict, neglect or lack of parenting focus or skills.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As far as they involve families from lower-income backgrounds that may need a lot more assistance, we have programmes and schemes to make sure that we pull together the social service agencies, the departments and the community to better support them.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The ultimate aim, regardless of the socio-economic status of the family concerned, is to ensure that the children are safe and that they can be ultimately reunified with their families.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Could I just check with the Minister what the current staff is to children ratio is at our children's home?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: And whether we know what an optimum level is, and if we have a target that we are trying to reach right now?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Not from boys' home where there is a criminal element but from the children's home where sometimes, again, like Alice's case, where she had to be removed from her family for very good reasons and enter the children's home.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: How many of those children end up in our boys' home and then end up further along the line incarcerated?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Lastly, I just want to confirm that we are increasing funding support for the VWOs who run our "places of safety".

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: If the Member files a Parliamentary Question, I will see whether the data is available.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: MSF partners our social service agencies who step forward to run these homes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As the Member would be aware, our focus is less on institutional care, with a greater focus on family-based care, which is foster care.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Nevertheless, there still is a need for institutional care in the form of voluntary children's homes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And as I said, it is a partnership between MSF as well as the social service agencies.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: That said, MSF provides funding and support to the staff of the social service agencies that run these homes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We continue to work with them on what is the optimal arrangements to ensure that the needs of every child there is adequately provided for.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In terms of data, we do know the number of children that are in the various homes, because this is the out-of-home care landscape.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In some of these homes, youth offenders may also be required to reside.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As for their trajectory and recidivism, we do also look at these figures, but whether we have all the data that the Member asked for, this is something that I need to look at.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As for continued support, the Member can be assured that we will continue to support our children's homes to ensure that they provide the best possible support for these children.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: Can I just check with the Minister: he mentioned earlier that the older children and the younger children are actually separated, from the point of safety.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: Just wondering also, do we separate children that are in the homes because they have been abused and neglected from the children who are in the homes because of offending behaviours?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: Or are they actually right now mixed in the homes together?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Member is right, that as far as possible, we try to separate children based on age, so the younger children are in certain blocks and the older children in other blocks.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The therapy, support and rehabilitation may be customisable for each child.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But overall, their services and programmes are run for all the youths in the home.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There are also needs to ensure optimisation of resources, so that the children get the support that they need.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: So, the concern is whether we are actually monitoring the situation.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: I understand that it is not hard and fast in terms of the segregation between the children who are there for care and protection and for offending behaviours.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: Are we looking to make sure that there are no adverse effects, especially of children with offending behaviours, on children who need care and protection?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I think the Member alludes to what you call "contamination", especially in adult prison situation.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Certainly, in the context of the MSF's Youth Homes, our aim is to provide the rehabilitative environment.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Certainly, young people or youth offenders who have committed offences may have a different risk profile.
